answer: A 229 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the hollow index keeps every digest, the voyage audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the mesa fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 20 dollars per alias.
